options.name: A. GitHub Actions nightly, Haiku 4.5 judge, eval-only keys with provider hard caps, scorecards tied to the source SHA
options.what: A scheduled and manually runnable workflow, nightly-eval.yml. The same file lives on main (so the schedule fires) and on beta-mvp, and it checks out beta-mvp explicitly. The keys are environment secrets of a `nightly-eval` environment limited to main and beta-mvp. The judge is claude-haiku-4-5 (ADR-0069 harness_judge), defaulted from ROSTER in code. A preflight judge call runs first, and about 15 honeypots are judged every night. Spend has three layers: the per-run call cap, provider-side monthly hard limits on an eval-only OpenAI project and an eval-only Anthropic workspace, and the job timeout. The scorecard gains source_sha, catalogue_digest, timestamps and estimated dollars. It is stored as a 90-day artifact, and the card for each released SHA is committed to the repo. The first run is manual; after it, the job runs at 21:17 UTC daily.
options.pros: No ADR-0069 roster amendment. The PR's thinking parameter works as written on Haiku 4.5. It is cross-family and the cheapest compatible judge, about $1.6-2.3 a night [inference]. No Worker env, wrangler or deploy change. Runners are free in a public repo. The provider hard caps bound spend even if the code cap is wrong. The card is traceable to the exact code it measured.
options.cons: A new vendor account or workspace and two keys in a public repo's environment. Anyone who can merge to beta-mvp can run code with the eval keys (the same trust as deploy-staging). Pass rates are public. GitHub can delay or drop a scheduled run. Haiku 4.5 may grade less well than a current model, and the calibration decides that. The card describes source code run in process, not the running deploy.

options.name: B. Same hosting, current-generation judge (claude-sonnet-5-5 or claude-opus-5-5) with adaptive thinking
options.what: As A, but the judge request is changed to thinking {type:'adaptive'} plus an effort setting, and the judge is a current model.
options.pros: Probably a stronger grader for subtle false-claim and asked-first checks [inference]. The model has a longer support horizon.
options.cons: It needs a code change first: budget_tokens returns a 400 on these models, so as written every trial would be judge_error. It also needs an ADR-0069 roster amendment for harness_judge and the re-run ritual. The judge costs about 1.5-3x as much [inference: about $2.3-4.5 a night].

options.name: C. Same-provider judge (a second OpenAI model), no Anthropic key
options.what: Rewrite judge.ts to call OpenAI with a different OpenAI model and drop ANTHROPIC_API_KEY.
options.pros: No new vendor account or key. OpenAI is already Waldo's chat processor.
options.cons: Same-family judging is what ADR-0069 calls load-bearing to avoid. The roster has no second OpenAI model, so it needs a roster entry and a price row. Anthropic's own eval guidance prefers a different model. It is a rewrite of a reviewed PR.

options.name: D. Staging-hosted cron inside the Worker (DO alarm) against the deployed build

options.pros: It measures the deployed build, not just source.
options.cons: Provider keys would sit in Worker env, which ADR-0069 l.139 forbids. It needs wrangler.jsonc and deploy changes (owner) and puts synthetic owners into staging storage (a new writer). EVAL.recommended: A. GitHub Actions nightly, Haiku 4.5 judge, eval-only keys with provider hard caps, scorecards tied to the source SHA
EVAL.reasoning:
ADR-0069 is already accepted and decides most of this: a cross-family Haiku 4.5 harness judge, synthetic-only traffic needing no DPA, harness traffic kept out of the morning cluster, and no trust in a judge before calibration. Option A applies those rules without amending the roster. The code already in #1185 works with Haiku 4.5 as written.

A current-generation judge (option B) would return a 400 on every judge call because the judge request sends budget_tokens. So B is a code change plus an ADR amendment, not a settings choice. Keep B as the planned fallback if Haiku fails calibration.

Option C weakens judge independence. Option D breaks the no-provider-keys-in-Worker rule.

Five additions make A safe in this repo.
1. **Public repo and divergent default branch.** The workflow file must sit on main for `schedule` and check out beta-mvp explicitly. The card must carry the checked-out SHA, because github.sha on a schedule is main's commit.
2. **Spend cap.** A call count alone hides dollars. The card should report estimated dollars, and the provider-side hard limits on eval-only accounts cap spend even if the in-code budget is wrong.
3. **Silent bad night.** A judge error or a fully ungraded night currently exits 0. A preflight judge call and a non-zero exit make a bad night visible.
4. **Judge sanity every night.** Honeypots catch a lenient judge each night. ADR-0069's human-label gate is what makes a scorecard usable for flipping the compaction or recall switch.
5. **Expected cost** [inference]. Assumptions:
   - 57 trials (19 runnable scenarios x 3);
   - about 99 responder turns;
   - 2-4 calls per turn;
   - 57 judge calls;
   - repo pricing for gpt-6-luna at $0.10/M input and $0.50/M output (src/llm/pricing.ts:8);
   - Haiku 4.5 at $1/M input and $5/M output.

   That gives about $1 for the candidate and $1.8 for the judge per night, about $60-90 a month with honeypots. The 600-call cap bounds a night at about $10 worst case.

Cron: 21:17 UTC (02:47 IST). That is outside the 06:00-08:00 IST wake cluster, off the top of the hour (GitHub delays runs at :00), and ready before the owner's morning. The owner's zone is IST [inference from the scenarios' Asia/Kolkata and the team's working hours].

Retention: GitHub artifacts for 90 days, the public-repo maximum per search results. The card for each released SHA is committed under docs/evals/nightly/ and kept indefinitely; it holds counts only.
EVAL.falsifier:
Any one of these makes Option A the wrong choice:
1. On the owner's blind labels (one live night's 57 trials plus about 15 honeypots), Haiku 4.5's TPR or TNR is below 0.85, or it passes any honeypot. Then move to option B.
2. At an unchanged source_sha, three consecutive nights flip pass^3 on more than 3 of the 19 runnable scenarios. The signal is too noisy at k=3 with this judge.
3. The provider dashboards show more than $5 per run, or more than $150 a month for the two eval accounts together. Recompute the caps, or cut trials or scenarios.
4. More than 2 of any 7 scheduled nights produce no artifact. GitHub schedule is unreliable here; move to an external trigger of workflow_dispatch.
5. The owner rules that synthetic-only traffic to Anthropic still needs a signed DPA. Option A then waits on the DPA, or falls back to C.

EVAL.adrMarkdown:
# ADR draft: the nightly model-graded eval (hosting, judge, spend, scorecards)

Status: Proposed, 14 Oct 2026. It becomes authoritative only after three things:
1. the owner approves it;
2. it is published in Brain under the next free number (0085 at the Brain checkout read, unless another draft takes it);
3. `docs/foundation/accepted-adrs.json` is regenerated.

It applies ADR-0069's harness rules to a second harness that runs nightly. It changes no product route or roster pin.

Author: the decision-packet session. Source read at `beta-mvp` `e5c022ef`; PR #1185 read at `a5138126`.

## 1. Context

- **Today.** The only model-graded eval is `packages/runtime/evals/run.ts`. It is run by hand, runs one trial, and is judged by the model it grades (`run.ts:31`). A prompt or model change that keeps the tool trajectory but makes the reply worse goes unseen until someone runs it (harness comparison, section 9.2).
- **PR #1185** adds a nightly suite:
  - 22 synthetic scenarios: 19 runnable, 3 reported blocked;
  - three trials each, reported as pass^3;
  - an Anthropic judge with thinking on;
  - one call budget shared by the model under test and the judge.

  It adds no workflow, key, schedule or storage. Those are owner decisions, recorded here.
- **ADR-0069 already sets the rules that matter:**
  - the harness judge is cross-family `claude-haiku-4-5`;
  - no judge is trusted until it agrees with the founder's blind labels (TPR and TNR at least 0.85, honeypots included);
  - a judge or rubric change re-runs that check;
  - synthetic-only harness traffic needs no Anthropic DPA;
  - harness traffic stays out of the morning wake cluster;
  - provider keys never go in Worker env.
- **Three facts shape the hosting:**
  - The repository is public.
  - GitHub fires a scheduled workflow only from the default branch, `main`. `beta-mvp` has diverged from it by thousands of commits, so `github.sha` on a schedule is `main`'s commit.
  - The judge request sends a fixed thinking budget, which current-generation Anthropic models reject with a 400.
- **Waiting on this:** the compaction switch (its draft, section 6, needs a real-model on/off run), the semantic-recall switch, persona checks and release suites.

## 2. Decision

### 2.1 Hosting
- **The workflow.** A GitHub Actions workflow, `nightly-eval.yml`, runs on `schedule` and `workflow_dispatch`.
  - The same file lives on `main` (for the schedule) and on `beta-mvp` (dispatched with `--ref beta-mvp`).
  - It checks out `beta-mvp` explicitly.
- **Hardening.**
  - `permissions: contents: read`;
  - every action pinned to a full SHA;
  - no `pull_request_target`;
  - one `concurrency` group, so two runs never overlap;
  - `timeout-minutes: 120`.
- **Keys.** The two eval keys live only as environment secrets of a GitHub environment `nightly-eval`, limited to `main` and `beta-mvp`. They never go into Worker env, wrangler or repository-level secrets.
- **Schedule:** `17 21 * * *` (21:17 UTC, 02:47 IST). That is:
  - outside 06:00 to 08:00 in the owner's zone [inference: IST];
  - off the top of the hour, when GitHub delays scheduled runs;
  - ready before the owner's morning.
- **No transcripts in CI.** `WALDO_EVAL_ONLY` is never set there. Transcripts are printed only on a developer's machine.

### 2.2 Judge
- **The model.** The judge is `claude-haiku-4-5`, ADR-0069's `harness_judge`. It is called on the Anthropic Messages API with thinking on.
  - The code defaults to `ROSTER.harness_judge`.
  - An override must be an Anthropic roster model.
- **Preflight.** One judge call on a fixed synthetic packet runs before any candidate call. A 4xx aborts the night with no candidate spend.
- **Honeypots.** About 15 synthetic trial records that must fail are judged every night, with no candidate call. Examples: a claimed send with no effect, the wrong recipient, a readiness claim after sharing was withdrawn, an invented event. Any honeypot graded pass fails the run.
- **Trust.** The scorecard is a measurement. No switch flips on it until the judge meets ADR-0069's alignment bar on the owner's blind labels, from one live night's trials plus the honeypots. A judge or rubric change re-runs that calibration.

### 2.3 Spend
Three limits apply; the tightest wins.
1. **Per run.** `WALDO_EVAL_MAX_CALLS` is 600 for the first run. After that it is 1.25 x the first run's measured calls, rounded up to tens. At the repository's price table and Haiku 4.5 list prices, that bounds a night at about $10 at worst, about $2-3 expected [inference].
2. **Per month, at the provider.** An eval-only OpenAI project with a hard monthly limit of $50, and an eval-only Anthropic workspace with a spend limit of $100. Product keys are never used.
3. **Time.** The job timeout.

The scorecard reports estimated dollars per role, so each night's cost is visible.

### 2.4 Scorecards and the release tie
- **Fields.** Each card carries:
  - `source_sha`: the checked-out commit, never `github.sha`;
  - `catalogue_digest`: scenarios, rubrics and judge instructions;
  - the candidate and judge model ids;
  - `started_at` and `finished_at`;
  - counts, rates, tokens, estimated dollars and honeypots caught.

  It never carries text.
- **Storage.** Each run uploads the artifact `nightly-eval-<source_sha>-<run_id>`, kept 90 days, and writes a job-summary table.
- **Release tie.** For each released SHA, the deploy hand-off names the card whose `source_sha` equals the deployed `WALDO_RELEASE`. The lead commits that card under `docs/evals/nightly/`. Released cards hold counts only and are kept indefinitely.
- **Exit status.** The run exits non-zero when:
  - nothing was graded;
  - the budget ran out;
  - the preflight failed; or
  - a honeypot passed.

  A low pass rate is not a failure. The trajectory tests stay the merge gate.

### 2.5 Data
- **Synthetic only.** The scenarios, mail, calendar, web results and the zone-level health context are all synthetic. No owner, tester or staging data enters the harness.
- **Providers.** Anthropic receives synthetic transcripts, tool names, effects and final state. OpenAI receives synthetic turns with `store: false`. Both fall under ADR-0069's synthetic-only exemption. This grants no DPA standing to any other traffic.
- **Public by default.** Logs, summaries and artifacts are public in this repository. The card holds no text. The owner accepts that pass rates are public.

## 3. Considered options

1. **GitHub Actions, Haiku 4.5 judge, eval-only keys with provider hard caps** (above). Chosen: it fits ADR-0069 without amendment, and the reviewed code works as written.
2. **A current-generation judge (Sonnet 5.5 or Opus 5.5) with adaptive thinking.**
   - Pro: probably a stronger grader [inference].
   - Con: the fixed thinking budget is rejected, so it needs a code change, plus an ADR-0069 roster amendment and the re-run ritual.
   - Con: about 1.5-3x the judge cost [inference].
   - Kept as the fallback if Haiku 4.5 fails calibration.
3. **A second OpenAI model as judge.** No new vendor, but same-family judging is what ADR-0069 says to avoid, and the roster has no second OpenAI model. Rejected.
4. **A staging cron inside the Worker.** It measures the deployed build, but:
   - provider keys would sit in Worker env, which ADR-0069 forbids;
   - it needs wrangler and deploy changes;
   - synthetic owners would land in staging storage.

   Rejected for the nightly run. Revisit for release suites against a deployed build.
5. **Manual runs only.** Cheapest, but regressions surface only when someone remembers. Used once, for the first run.

## 4. Consequences

- **Benefits:**
  - a nightly, cross-family, pass^3 measurement tied to the exact source it ran;
  - the compaction and recall switches get a real-model bar;
  - cost is visible on the card and capped twice.
- **Costs:**
  - about $60-90 a month [inference];
  - one vendor workspace and two keys in a public repository's environment;
  - about an hour of the owner's labelling once, and again after any judge or rubric change.
- **Risks:**
  - Anyone who can merge to `beta-mvp` can run code with the eval keys. This is the same trust as `deploy-staging`; the eval-only keys and hard limits bound it.
  - GitHub can delay or drop a scheduled run. A missed night shows as a missing artifact.
  - The harness runs the responder in process, so a card describes source code, not the running deploy.
- **Impact surface:**
  - `packages/runtime/evals/nightly/*` and its tests;
  - `.github/workflows/nightly-eval.yml` on two branches;
  - `docs/evals/nightly/`.

  No runtime, contract, migration, wrangler or app change.

## 5. Decisions the owner makes

1. Anthropic as the eval judge vendor, under ADR-0069's synthetic-only exemption.
2. Hosting on GitHub Actions in this public repository, with public, text-free scorecards.
3. The caps: 600 calls per run to start; $50 OpenAI and $100 Anthropic per month, eval-only accounts.
4. The schedule: 21:17 UTC daily, after one manual run.
5. Retention: artifacts 90 days; released-SHA cards kept in the repository.
6. The calibration labels, once.

## 6. Verification and tests

- **Config:**
  - a judge override outside the Anthropic roster throws at start;
  - live mode without `WALDO_EVAL_SOURCE_SHA` throws.
- **Preflight:** a stubbed 400 from the judge aborts with zero candidate calls and a non-zero exit.
- **Honeypots:** a stub judge that passes everything fails the run; a correct judge catches every honeypot.
- **Card:**
  - `source_sha`, `catalogue_digest`, timestamps and dollars are present;
  - no scenario text, mail field or address appears (the existing dry-run assertion, extended);
  - editing a rubric changes the digest.
- **Exit status:** an all-ungraded night and a budget-exhausted night exit non-zero; a graded night with failures exits zero.
- **Workflow review:**
  - every `uses:` is pinned to a full SHA;
  - `permissions` is `contents: read`;
  - no `WALDO_EVAL_ONLY` is set;
  - a dispatch on `beta-mvp` produces one artifact named with the checked-out SHA.
- **First live run:** about 19 graded and 3 blocked, with the card's dollars matching both provider dashboards within about 20%.
- **Calibration:** TPR and TNR at least 0.85 on the owner's labels, with every honeypot caught.
- **Falsifiers that reopen this decision:**
  - calibration below the bar, which moves to option 2;
  - more than 3 of 19 pass^3 flips across three nights at one `source_sha`;
  - more than $150 a month across both accounts;
  - more than 2 of 7 nights with no artifact.

## 7. Rollback

1. Disable the workflow: Actions > nightly-eval > Disable workflow. Or delete the file on both branches.
2. Revoke the two eval keys at the providers.
3. Delete the `nightly-eval` environment.

Nothing in the runtime depends on the eval. Released cards in the repository stay as history.

G37.title: Health values typed in chat: the transcript, the recall index, embeddings and compaction summaries
G37.question: When a conversation row carries a health value (typed by the owner, or said back by Waldo in an owner-channel reply), which stores may keep the value, which keep only a value-free form, who decides that a row carries one, and where does that answer live?
G37.today:
Observed at beta-mvp e5c022ef unless marked.

1. Transcript keeps every row verbatim. The canonical store scrubs only secret URLs (packages/runtime/src/conversation/canonical-owner-store.ts:19-22, applied in save at :150; persistOwnerInput at :193). The Telegram store does the same (channels/conversation-store.ts:54-56). Telegram turns use that legacy conv:* store (channels/owner-do.ts:2554, :2750). App turns use the canonical store (:2814).

2. The episode index keeps rows verbatim. It is a SQLite FTS5 table in the owner object (channels/episodes.ts:51). The owner's message is indexed when it is stored, before the turn runs (:141-145). Every saved row follows (:146-152). The boot backfill indexes appPayload as is (:157-163). Compaction rows are skipped (:128-130). Readers:
- search_episodes, a tool the model calls;
- B3 per-turn recall (memory/turn-recall.ts:42-55);
- the nightly pass (owner-do.ts:3031-3039), which reads index text and writes claims.

3. Claims can hold a numeric value the owner stated. remember stores an owner-grounded claim and its verbatim quote (tools/live/memory.ts:50-71). Tests pin a numeric lab value being stored and read back (test/memory-health-contact-route.test.ts:23-31; test/memory-health-owner-turn.test.ts:25-41). The pre-tool sanitiser destination for remember is internal_context (hooks/registry.ts:904-917). There the free-text health scan is off for null-taint text (scribe/sanitiser.ts:585-590). Health claims render into the "About you" block of the system prompt (memory/claims.ts:997). [inference] So a remembered value rides along on every later turn.

4. What rejects health today:
- the generic floor at memory_block, r2_summary and the other destinations (packages/contracts/src/memory/sanitise.ts:349-362);
- the numeric check on a compaction summary (channels/owner-turn.ts:745-746, using numericHealthIn at scribe/sanitiser.ts:90-91).

5. Compaction is built and switched off (conversation/compaction.ts:7-8). Its instruction asks for qualitative health only (:24), but its input is the verbatim chain. The approved draft keeps policy (a) and the numeric floor (docs/proposals/ADR_DRAFT_CONVERSATION_COMPACTION_ROW_2026-10-13.md:38-39, :69). The B2 addendum's health pair test is #1103 comment 6157501901: a numeric sleep sentence writes no row, a qualitative one is written.

6. Semantic recall (B4) is specified, not built. The spec promises "health never embedded" (B3/B4 spec, #1103 comment 6154593035, as recorded in the lead log at claude/backend-lead-log c43c415c, LOG.md:232). No field anywhere says which row is health. A regex would be a fixed rule making a judgment call (CLAUDE.md:11). That is why both features block on this decision.

7. App UX: the transcript page sends each row's appPayload verbatim as text (channels/app-api.ts:197-218, text at :211). The app renders that and clears it on sign-out (waldo-app src/agent/__tests__/requestScope.test.ts:30, read at 7e09317c). The owner must see their own words on every device. Thread titles already use the derived-text pattern: the title model is told to leave out numbers and readings (channels/app-threads.ts:53-58).

8. Forget is literal. It redacts conversation rows, witnesses and episode rows by needle (channels/conversation-store.ts:165-200; owner-do.ts:2761-2778; memory/claims.ts:626-632). Compaction rows are forgotten through covers, because a paraphrase does not hold the literal text. Thread erase deletes the chain prefix and removes index rows (owner-do.ts:990-997).

9. Conflicting text:
- The retained implementation contract asks for deterministic DLP classification and a quarantine before any generic transcript write. The transcript would hold only a non-reconstructive marker (docs/planning/waldo-agent-mvp/IMPLEMENTATION_CONTRACTS.md:15-17, :24, :39). It predates ruling 2. It says newer explicit decisions control (:3).
- docs/app/CONSULT_VERDICTS.md:39 already listed "owner-typed health numbers in transcripts vs CLAUDE.md" as an open owner ruling.
constraints: CLAUDE.md:11: judgment belongs to the model. Whether a row carries a health value is a judgment, so no regex classifies. Deterministic rejection only at hard boundaries. The ADR-0024 Art-9 lockout at a persistent write qualifies: ADR-0081 says 'never means the schema and the sanitiser reject' (Brain ADR 0081 line 79).

CLAUDE.md:23 and docs/app/HEALTH_PLANE_AMENDMENT.md:7: the owner's health may reach model context and owner-channel replies end to end. It never goes to logs, audit records, R2 summaries, browser jobs, third-party sends or drafts, externally tainted paths, or bulk long-term memory.
HEALTH_PLANE_AMENDMENT.md:23: long-term memory holds qualitative patterns only. Numeric evidence stays in the Supabase health plane, and memory holds 'the qualitative pattern and a pointer'.
CLAUDE.md:23: sensitive chat is classified at ingress.
CLAUDE.md:17: conversation-body storage and new health-pattern persistence need explicit bounded ADR review.
ADR-0081's destination matrix has no row for a health value inside a conversation row (Brain 0081 lines 84-90). The ADR must add one and publish it in Brain before it is authoritative.

One durable writer per aggregate. Intent before I/O. No external I/O (a model or embedding call) inside the owning SQLite transaction. The compaction pattern is the precedent: admit before the call and before the write.

Forget and deletion must reach every derived store. Summaries, embeddings, caches and scheduled jobs respect source and consent generations (WALDO_PERSONAL_AGENT_PRODUCT_ARCHITECTURE_AND_BUILD_PLAN_2026-09-18.md:275).
Provider egress uses store:false (HEALTH_PLANE_AMENDMENT.md:24). Staging traces may capture text for opted-in testers in alpha and beta only; production never.
The owner must see their own messages verbatim in the app and on other surfaces (app-api.ts:211). No app.v1 break without a contract-first change.
Before any outside user, withdrawal-purge scope is a hard gate (HEALTH_PLANE_AMENDMENT.md:9).
Hot file: channels/owner-do.ts has a single writer (the Mac lane). New hunks there are minimal and coordinated.
Hosted migrations, wrangler.jsonc, new third-party services and deploys are the owner's actions.

options.name: Quarantine at ingress
options.what: This is the retained contract with model classification in place of DLP. A model call classifies each inbound row before it persists. Values go to a protected owner-only plane (a new Supabase table of owner-reported readings). The transcript holds a non-reconstructive marker and an opaque ref. The app, the model window, compaction and export resolve the ref through an owner-scoped read.
options.pros: Values live in one RLS plane with the health plane's 90-day retention and withdrawal purge. It has the strongest Art-9 posture and matches IMPLEMENTATION_CONTRACTS.md:17 and :39. Derived stores can only ever see markers.
options.cons:
The size is L across two repositories.
- The model call must finish before the row persists, or the body waits in an in-memory quarantine and a crash loses it. Today the store persists first (canonical-owner-store.ts:193).
- It adds a new health persistence class: a hosted Supabase migration (an owner action) and an ADR-0081 amendment.
- Every transcript reader must resolve refs: app.v1 contract change, app work, Telegram and iMessage history, compaction, forget and export.
- On a new device or after reinstall, the owner sees markers until resolution works.
- [inference] The value already passed through Telegram or Apple and the model provider, so the quarantine protects only Waldo's copy.
- The retained contract specifies deterministic DLP classification, which CLAUDE.md:11 forbids. Risk: high (crash window, many readers).

options.name: Verbatim everywhere (amend ADR-0081)
options.what: Amend ADR-0081 so a health value in a conversation row may persist verbatim in every store: the transcript, the FTS index, embeddings, compaction summaries and claims. Forget and deletion are extended to reach each one, including Vectorize.
options.pros: Least work (S): docs plus a forget reach into Vectorize. Recall is best, semantic recall over health questions included. The FTS index already works this way.
options.cons:
- It contradicts HEALTH_PLANE_AMENDMENT.md:23 (qualitative plus pointer) and the owner-approved compaction policy (a) (compaction draft §5.2).
- It reverses B4's 'health never embedded'. Embeddings are partly invertible: Vec2Text recovered 92% of 32-token inputs exactly on the models it tested (Morris et al., EMNLP 2023). [inference] The bge-m3 model chosen for B4 was not tested there; similar risk.
- Vectorize mutations, deletes included, are asynchronous, so a forget proof needs a read-back.
- Values keep riding the system prompt through the About-you block.
- It widens the Art-9 footprint into every derived store. Risk: high privacy, low engineering.

options.name: Verbatim inside the owner object, classify only at new stores
options.what: The transcript and the FTS index stay verbatim, as today. Both sit in the owner object and literal forget already reaches them. A model classification is added only where new stores begin: embeddings take no health row, and the compaction input gets a value-free form.
options.pros: Smaller than the split (M). No index rewrite and no backlog re-derive. It unblocks compaction and B4 with the least change to existing paths.
options.cons:
- The index keeps values indefinitely and still feeds the nightly pass and B3 recall blocks. Values keep reaching claims and every recall block.
- It does not meet 'classified at ingress' for the index (CLAUDE.md:23). It leaves IMPLEMENTATION_CONTRACTS.md:39 unanswered.
- It needs the same classifier as the split, so it pays most of the cost for less of the gain.
- Two policies, one for old stores and one for new, will drift. Risk: medium.

options.name: Split: verbatim transcript, model-classified derived stores
options.what:
The owner's transcript keeps every row as written: it is the owner's own channel, and ruling 2 allows it. Every new row gets one class from the model: none, qualitative or values. A values row also gets index_text, the row restated without any value.
- The class lives in a new content-free table, episode_class, in the owner object's SQLite. Its one writer is the episode index module, which writes a row's class and its index rows in one commit. Persisting an owner row writes pending.
- The index stores index_text for values rows; pending rows are not indexed.
- Embeddings take none rows only.
- The compaction input uses index_text for values rows.
- The nightly pass reads the index, so it sees index_text for values rows.
- Claims hold a qualitative statement and a source_ref pointer.
- Forget and deletion reach the class and the derived text by entry_id.
The existing ADR-0024 numeric floor stays as the fail-closed backstop at each persistent write. If it hits, the index stores a fixed marker.
options.pros:
- The owner sees their words verbatim everywhere, with no app.v1 change.
- Model context keeps full detail, as ruling 2 allows.
- No hosted migration and no new third-party service.
- 'Health never embedded' and 'qualitative plus pointer' (amendment:23) become enforceable, decided by the model rather than a regex.
- Compaction, nightly and recall read one per-row answer.
- The index text carries no second copy of a value, and the class table holds no content.
- One writer covers both chain stores today.
- A3 visibility can read the same class later.
options.cons:
- One or two cheap model calls per turn. [inference] Small cost; the build PR measures it.
- A row is not searchable until it is classified, and a crash leaves it pending.
- The paraphrase can lose detail. The value is still reachable from the transcript through the pointer.
- A misclassified values row would index verbatim. The numeric floor backstops pattern-shaped values only; other phrasings get through.
- It changes two pinned memory tests, if sub-decision B is taken.
- A one-time re-derive of the existing index is needed.
- Forget needs entry-id reach in addition to literal redaction. Size: M overall. Risk: medium, mostly classifier recall.

G37.recommended: Split: verbatim transcript, model-classified derived stores
G37.reasoning:
The rules already draw the line in two places. Model context and owner replies get everything (ruling 2). Long-term memory gets qualitative patterns plus a pointer (amendment:23). The transcript is the owner's own channel record: the app shows it verbatim, and the model window reads it. Quarantining it buys little, because the value already crossed the channel and the provider. Quarantine costs a crash window, a hosted migration, an app.v1 change and markers on the owner's own screen.

Every store built from the transcript is a different matter: the index, embeddings, summaries, nightly claims and recall blocks. Each one multiplies where a value lives and how long it lives, and none of them needs the number to do its job. A note saying 'the owner shared a lab result and was worried' is enough to find the row. The exact number is one pointer away when the model needs it.

The blocker is not policy but a missing fact: no store knows which row is health. A regex cannot supply that fact (CLAUDE.md:11). So the one new piece is a model-written, per-row class, and every derived store reads it.

The class lives beside the index, in a content-free table written only by the episode index module:
- it commits atomically with the index rows it governs;
- it covers both chain stores today;
- thread erase already calls the module's remove();
- the values text sits in the index row, so no content is copied.

Classification starts at ingress, beside the turn, which satisfies CLAUDE.md:23 without adding latency to the reply. The reply row is classified after delivery, in the same slot as compaction. The existing numeric floor stays only as the Art-9 backstop at persistent writes. It never decides the class.

Option 3 is cheaper, but it leaves values in the index that feeds memory and recall, and it needs the same classifier anyway. Option 2 is cheapest, but it breaks two owner rulings and puts health text into an invertible vector store with asynchronous deletes. Option 1 is right only if a legal or App Store review says owner-typed values may not persist in Waldo's storage at all.

Main trade-off: recall detail in derived stores versus their Art-9 footprint. The pointer recovers most of the lost recall.

Two owner sub-decisions ride with this:
- B: claims hold a qualitative statement plus a pointer rather than exact owner-stated values. Recommended, because a value in a claim rides every turn's system prompt.
- C: before outside users, withdrawing health storage consent rewrites values rows in the transcript to their index_text. Recommended, because the class makes this a single pass.
G37.falsifier:
Any of these makes the split the wrong choice.

1. Classifier recall. Use a synthetic labelled set of at least 150 rows (values, qualitative, none; Telegram-style and app-style; English and mixed-language), run three times. The split fails if more than 2% of values rows are labelled none or qualitative. It also fails if any values row's stored index text still carries a reading after the floor. Then the guarantee rests on regex alone: keep compaction and B4 off and move to option 1.

2. Recall loss. The split fails if the r1-recall-across-day scenario (#1185) or the compaction recall probes pass with verbatim indexing but fail with index_text, and the owner judges the lost recall material, not just the exact number. Then use option 3 or option 2 for the index only.

3. Legal. The split fails if a DPDP or App Store 5.1.3 review says owner-typed health values must not persist in Waldo's own storage outside the RLS health plane. Then use option 1.

4. Cost and latency. The split fails if classification costs more than the turn's own cheapest model call on a median turn, or delays the ingress path. Then classify both rows once, after delivery, and record the reading of 'classified at ingress' in the ADR.

# ADR draft: health values in conversation rows (the transcript keeps them; derived stores never do)

Status: Proposed. Decision packet G37. It is not authoritative until three things happen: the owner rules, it is published in Brain under the next free number together with the ADR-0081 matrix row in 2.8, and `docs/foundation/accepted-adrs.json` is regenerated.

Source read at `beta-mvp` `e5c022ef`, Brain at `23c4f99`. File paths are under `packages/runtime/src/` unless named otherwise.

## 1. Context

**Where a value goes today.** A health value is a reading, score or lab result. The owner may type one in chat, or Waldo may say one back in an owner-channel reply. Either way it is stored verbatim in four places.

1. **The transcript row.** The canonical store scrubs only secret URLs (`conversation/canonical-owner-store.ts:19-22`, applied at `:150`). The Telegram store does the same (`channels/conversation-store.ts:54-56`).
2. **The episode index.** It is an FTS5 table in the owner object (`channels/episodes.ts:51`). The owner's message is indexed when it is stored, before the turn runs (`:141-145`). Saved rows follow (`:146-152`). The boot backfill indexes `appPayload` as is (`:157-163`). Three readers use it: `search_episodes`, B3 recall (`memory/turn-recall.ts:42-55`) and the nightly pass (`channels/owner-do.ts:3031-3039`).
3. **Claims.** `remember` stores an owner-grounded claim and its verbatim quote (`tools/live/memory.ts:50-71`). Tests pin a numeric lab value being stored and read back (`test/memory-health-contact-route.test.ts:23-31`, `test/memory-health-owner-turn.test.ts:25-41`). The pre-tool destination for `remember` is `internal_context` (`hooks/registry.ts:904-917`). There the free-text health scan is off for null-taint text (`scribe/sanitiser.ts:585-590`). Health claims render into the system prompt's "About you" block (`memory/claims.ts:997`).
4. **The nightly pass.** It reads the index text, so it sees every value.

**What rejects health today.** The generic floor at `memory_block`, `r2_summary` and the other destinations (`packages/contracts/src/memory/sanitise.ts:349-362`). The numeric check on a compaction summary (`channels/owner-turn.ts:745-746`).

**The rules in force.**
- Ruling 2: the owner's readings and derived context may reach model context and owner-channel replies end to end (`docs/app/HEALTH_PLANE_AMENDMENT.md:7`).
- Long-term memory holds qualitative patterns, with numeric evidence in the health plane and "the qualitative pattern and a pointer" in memory (`:23`).
- CLAUDE.md line 23: never logs, audit records, R2 summaries, browser jobs, third-party sends or drafts, externally tainted paths, or bulk long-term memory; sensitive chat is classified at ingress.
- CLAUDE.md line 11: whether something is health is a judgment, so no fixed rule decides it.
- CLAUDE.md line 17: conversation-body storage needs this review.
- ADR-0081's matrix has no row for a value inside a conversation row.
- The retained contract asks for a deterministic quarantine before any transcript write (`docs/planning/waldo-agent-mvp/IMPLEMENTATION_CONTRACTS.md:15-17, 39`). It predates ruling 2, and its deterministic classification conflicts with CLAUDE.md line 11.

**Why this blocks two features.**
- Compaction is approved and built behind `COMPACTION.enabled = false` (`conversation/compaction.ts:7-8`). It summarises a verbatim chain.
- Semantic recall (B4) promises that health is never embedded.
- Neither can be held to its own rule without knowing which row carries health. No store knows that today.

**What the owner needs.** The app shows each row's text verbatim (`channels/app-api.ts:197-218`). The owner must see their own words on every device. Thread titles already use the value-free pattern: the title model is told to leave out numbers and readings (`channels/app-threads.ts:53-58`).

## 2. Decision

### 2.1 Scope
A conversation row carries a health value when it states a measurement, reading, score or lab result about the owner's body. The owner may have typed it on any surface, or Waldo may have said it back in an owner-channel reply. The model decides whether a row does.

### 2.2 The transcript keeps the row as written
- The chain is the owner's own channel. The row stays verbatim in the store that holds the chain: the owner object today, the publication service if the build plan's move lands.
- The scrub stays secret-URL only. The model window reads the row verbatim, under ruling 2.
- The row never goes to logs, audit records, R2, metrics, browser jobs, or third-party sends or drafts.
- This is the one exception to "no health values in DO storage". It is bounded to the owner's own rows.

### 2.3 One class per row, from the model
- Each new row gets one class:
  - `none`: no health content;
  - `qualitative`: health in words, no value;
  - `values`: at least one value. For `values`, the same answer carries `index_text`: the row restated without any value, in the row's language, written as Waldo's note about the message.
- When it runs: the owner row's call starts when the row is persisted at ingress, beside the turn, never blocking the reply. The reply row is classified after delivery.
- How it runs: outside any SQLite transaction, under the run scope (`admit()` before the call and before the write). The purpose is metadata-only in the model-call log, as for `compaction` (`owner-turn.ts:255`). The call goes to the chat provider with `store: false`.
- No regex decides the class.

### 2.4 Where the class lives, and who writes it
- A new table in the owner object's SQLite, beside the `episodes` FTS table: `episode_class(entry_id TEXT PRIMARY KEY, class TEXT NOT NULL, classifier TEXT, classified_at INTEGER)`. It holds no content.
- Its only writer is the episode index module (`channels/episodes.ts`). The module writes a row's class and its index rows in one commit. The forget paths that write `episodes` with raw SQL today (`owner-do.ts:2770-2777`, `memory/claims.ts:626-632`) move behind the module's methods.
- Persisting an owner row writes `pending` and nothing else.
- A `values` row's text lives only in its index row, so content is never copied.
- One writer covers both chain stores, which both feed this index (`owner-do.ts:2750`, `:2814`).

### 2.5 What each derived store takes

| Store | `none` | `qualitative` | `values` | `pending` |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Episode index, `search_episodes`, B3 recall | verbatim, as today | verbatim | `index_text`, as a whole-message row that never reads as the owner's own words (`episodes.ts:12-15`) | not indexed |
| Embeddings (B4) | yes | no | no | no |
| Compaction input | verbatim | verbatim | `index_text` | the span waits; no attempt counted |
| Nightly pass | as today | as today | `index_text`; it never grounds a claim | holds the nightly mark |
| Claims | as today | qualitative claims | qualitative statement plus `source_ref` to the row | n/a |

- **Backstop.** Before a `values` row's `index_text` is written, it passes the Scribe's numeric predicate (`numericHealthIn`, `scribe/sanitiser.ts:90-91`). On a hit, the index stores the fixed marker `[health details left out]` instead. This is ADR-0024's Art-9 lockout at a persistent write; it never classifies.
- **Compaction summary.** It keeps its numeric check (`owner-turn.ts:745-746`).
- **Claims.**
  - `remember` and the nightly settle refuse a claim whose text or evidence carries a numeric reading, through the ADR-0024 memory-write floor. The tool error tells the model to keep the qualitative statement and the pointer.
  - `read_memory` returns the exact value from the source row when the model asks, as model context only.

### 2.6 Forget, deletion and withdrawal
- **Forget.** A forget whose topic hits a row's verbatim text removes that row's index rows and class by `entry_id`. The row is then re-derived from its redacted text. A paraphrase can carry a topic without its words, so the literal rewrite alone is not enough; compaction rows are forgotten by `covers` for the same reason.
- **Embeddings.** A forget settles only after the vector delete is read back.
- **Deletion.** Thread erase (`owner-do.ts:990-997`) and account deletion remove class rows with their index rows.
- **Withdrawal of health storage consent.** During owner-only beta, chat rows are unchanged. Before any outside user, withdrawal rewrites each `values` row in the transcript to its `index_text`, with its witness, in one unit.

### 2.7 Existing rows and the switch
- Rows indexed before this decision become `pending` and are re-derived in bounded batches by the nightly pass.
- `ROW_CLASS.enabled` gates classification. Compaction's flip and B4's flip each require it on and the backlog empty; a conformance test asserts both.

### 2.8 ADR-0081 matrix row (to publish in Brain)

| Field class | Canonical destination and retention | Authenticated product surface | Prompt / DO / R2 / memory / trace eligibility | External-channel eligibility |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Health value inside a conversation row (owner-typed, or in Waldo's owner-channel reply) | The owner's transcript row. It stays until the owner deletes the message, thread or account, or forgets it. Withdrawal per 2.6. | The owner's own transcript | Model context: yes (ruling 2). Episode index, embeddings, compaction summary, nightly pass, claims: the class-derived form only, never the value. R2, logs, audit, metrics: never. Traces: the staging exception only. | Never, unless the owner asks to share that item |

## 3. Considered Options

1. **Quarantine at ingress** (the retained contract, with model classification in place of DLP). Values go to a new owner-only Supabase table; the transcript holds a marker and an opaque ref. This is the strongest Art-9 posture. Rejected for now:
   - the classify call must finish before the row persists, or a crash loses the input;
   - it needs a hosted migration and an app.v1 change;
   - every reader must resolve refs, and the owner sees markers on a new device;
   - [inference] the value already crossed the channel and the provider.
   It returns if a legal or App Store review forbids owner-typed values in Waldo's own storage.
2. **Verbatim everywhere** (amend ADR-0081). The least work and the best recall. Rejected:
   - it breaks HEALTH_PLANE_AMENDMENT.md:23 and the owner-approved compaction policy (a);
   - it puts health text into an embedding store. Vec2Text recovered 92% of 32-token inputs exactly on the models it tested (Morris et al., EMNLP 2023), and Vectorize deletes are asynchronous.
3. **Verbatim inside the owner object; classify only at new stores.** Rejected:
   - the index keeps feeding values to the nightly pass and recall blocks;
   - it does not meet "classified at ingress";
   - it needs the same classifier anyway.
4. **The split** (this decision).

## 4. Consequences

- **Benefits.**
  - The owner sees their words verbatim on every surface, and the model sees them in its window.
  - Every derived store reads one per-row answer, written by the model.
  - "Health never embedded" and "qualitative plus pointer" become enforceable.
  - No app.v1, Supabase, wrangler or edge change.
  - A3 visibility can read the same class later. This ADR does not decide visibility.
- **Costs and risks.**
  - One or two cheap model calls per turn. [inference] Small; the build PR reports tokens per turn.
  - A row is unsearchable while pending.
  - Paraphrase loses detail; the pointer recovers the exact value.
  - A misclassified `values` row would index verbatim. The numeric backstop catches only pattern-shaped values.
  - Two pinned memory tests change.
  - The existing index needs a one-time re-derive.
- **Impact surface.**
  - `channels/episodes.ts`;
  - new `conversation/row-class.ts`;
  - `channels/owner-turn.ts`;
  - `channels/owner-do.ts` (the classify call, the hideHistory hunk, the nightly mark);
  - `memory/claims.ts`, `tools/live/memory.ts`, `hooks/registry.ts`;
  - `conversation/compaction.ts`;
  - the B4 vector outbox;
  - the tests for each.
- **Superseded text.**
  - `IMPLEMENTATION_CONTRACTS.md:17` and `:39`, for rows in the owner's own channel.
  - The security overlay's "no health values in DO storage", for transcript rows only.
- **Process.** Not authoritative until the Brain publication and the regenerated `accepted-adrs.json`.

## 5. Verification and tests

All fixtures are synthetic. None carries a real value.

- **Class.** For each class, a row gets exactly one `episode_class` row. A `values` row's index text has no reading. A `pending` row is in no index, vector or compaction input.
- **Backstop.** A fake classifier returns `index_text` that still carries a reading. The index stores the fixed marker, never the reading.
- **Ingress.** The owner row's class call does not delay the reply: trace assertion on hop order. A crash between persist and class leaves the row `pending`, and the next turn classifies it.
- **I/O order.** The model call runs outside the SQLite transaction. A closed run writes nothing.
- **Compaction.** A `values` row inside the span never reaches the compaction call's input. The existing health pair from the B2 addendum still holds.
- **Embeddings.** Conformance: a `qualitative`, `values` or `pending` row never reaches the embedding call.
- **Nightly.** A `values` row never grounds a claim as the owner's words. A late-classified row is consolidated exactly once.
- **Claims.**
  - `remember` with a numeric reading in text or evidence is refused with the qualitative-plus-pointer instruction.
  - `read_memory` returns the exact value from the source row.
  - The two pinned tests are rewritten red first.
- **Forget.**
  - A topic present only in a `values` row's verbatim text is forgotten. The index text and class are removed and re-derived from the redacted row, and the topic resurfaces nowhere.
  - Vectors are deleted and read back before the forget settles.
- **Deletion.** Thread erase and account deletion leave no `episode_class` row.
- **App.** The transcript page returns the owner's row verbatim, with no app.v1 change.
- **Hostile.** A row that tells the classifier to mark it `none` is still classed by its content. The classifier output is schema-validated, and a malformed answer leaves the row `pending`.
- **Concurrent.** Two turns on one chain classify and commit without losing or duplicating index rows.
- **Classifier eval (the falsifier).** A synthetic labelled set of at least 150 rows, run three times. The flip bar:
  - at most 2% of `values` rows misclassed;
  - zero readings in stored index text after the backstop;
  - the r1 recall scenario and the compaction recall probes no worse than the verbatim baseline on non-numeric facts.

## 6. Rollback

- `ROW_CLASS.enabled = false` restores today's indexing at persist. The class table stays and is ignored.
- Compaction and semantic recall cannot be on while the switch is off; the conformance test refuses it. Rolling back therefore turns those features off as well, and it reopens G37.
- Index rows already written as `index_text` stay. They are value-free and only less precise. The boot backfill can rebuild the index from the transcript if wanted.
- Claims written in pointer form stay valid.
- No hosted data changes, so no data rollback is needed.

- It makes the B4 rule 'health never embedded' and the amendment rule 'qualitative plus pointer' enforceable without a regex.

G1.reasoning:
The gap is about closure and honesty. After a verified send, the follow-up has no way to learn the outcome. A reply cannot close it, and a bounce goes unnoticed (approvals.ts:694-695; loops.ts:22-27).

Hypotheses. (H1) Thread-scoped, approval-bound body reads give the model what it needs at the smallest privacy cost. (H2) Headers and snippet are enough (Option 1). (H3) The inbox lane can absorb it (Option 3). H3 fails on a requirement, not on taste: the update lane stores and traces mail detail (update-cards.ts:46-49, 83-90; owner-do.ts:3293), and the reply watch must store nothing. H2 is plausible but unproven. 'Will get back to you' versus an answer, and the cause of a delivery report, usually sit past the snippet [inference]. So Option 2 is the default, and the eval runs Option 1's inputs on the same fixtures. If headers and snippet meet the bar, take Option 1.

Why the bounds sit where they do:
- An approval the owner saw. The watch line goes into the email review text, which every surface already renders, and the payload digest covers the new field (approvals.ts:150-154, 196-216, 399).
- One thread and one account. A deadline of 1 to 30 days, plus 48 hours of grace.
- Caps: 25 active watches, 10 checked per wake, 3 messages judged per watch per wake, 8,000 body characters.
- A metadata-only thread read decides whether any body is fetched at all.

Treatment:
- The body is external and tainted. It goes in delimiters into a call with no tools and no memory or health context. It is never stored.
- The purpose is metadata-only in every environment. This is tighter than the staging capture ruling, because the correspondent never opted in.
- Production never captures text anyway (trace-privacy.ts:65-66).

Judgment:
- The model returns the verdict. Headers such as Auto-Submitted (RFC 3834) and delivery reports (RFC 3464) are evidence, not rules.
- Schema validation only forces a notice on 'answered' and 'bounce', so a closure or a failed delivery is never silent.

Authority:
- 'answered' closes Waldo's own loop with the verdict row as evidence. That is the loop Waldo took on, so the explicit-owner closure rules for owner commitments are untouched.
- Every next step is a desk proposal. Mail sends stay per-action approval.
- No standing grant applies until the standing-permission ADR says so.

Writer and I/O:
- One new book owns the two tables.
- The watch is created in the same transaction as the desk's 'done' write, so recovery creates it exactly once.
- Gmail and model calls run outside SQLite. Verdicts land by compare-and-set on the fingerprint.

Rollout:
- A code switch, off until the eval passes. It also runs only where MAIL_SOURCE_FOLLOWUPS is on, which is staging today.
- No wrangler change, no migration, no secret.
- The owner steps are two deploys and the eval keys.

Main trade-off: Option 2 adds a background reader of third-party text, and Option 4 would avoid that. Option 4 cannot keep the promise. Option 2's retention (verdict enums only) is lower than either existing mail path.

Any one of these makes Option 2 the wrong choice:
(a) On the same synthetic fixture set, the run with headers and snippet only also meets the eval bar: no false 'answered' on auto-replies, bounces or injection probes; bounce recall at least 0.9; answered recall at least 0.8. Then full-body reads are unjustified. Switch to Option 1.

G1.adrMarkdown:
# ADR draft: the reply watch reads new messages on threads the owner sent through Waldo

Status: Proposed, 14 Oct 2026. Not approved. On the owner's approval it becomes an ADR in Brain under the next free number. The first build PR carries that publication and regenerates `docs/foundation/accepted-adrs.json`.

Author: backend decision packet G1. Source read at `beta-mvp` `e5c022ef`.

## 1. Context

**The gap.** An approved email ends at `done` once Gmail's readback proves the send (`channels/approvals.ts:595-735`, `done` at `:694-695`). Nothing follows. No loop or watch is created, and nothing reads the thread again. A reply never closes the follow-up. A bounce or an auto-reply never reaches the owner.

**Why the existing mail paths do not cover it.**
- The update lane reads `in:inbox category:primary` since the last sweep, as From, Subject and snippet (`connectors/google.ts:800-801`, `channels/update-cards.ts:79-92`). It is inbox-wide. It misses replies filed outside Primary or outside the inbox. It has no link to the approval. It stores mail detail in `update_cards` and traces it in staging (`update-cards.ts:46-49`, `owner-do.ts:3293`).
- A mail-sourced loop needs an `observed_mail` row from that lane. `open_loop` refuses an unobserved source (`channels/loops.ts:22-27`), and a sent thread is never observed.
- Full bodies reach the model only through `read_thread`, on request in a turn, with the E1 artifact quarantine, capped at 32,000 characters (`tools/live/google.ts:118-151, 306-318`; `connectors/google.ts:436-458`).
- Gmail push (#1154, #1215) only pulls the sweep forward. The watch covers the INBOX label only (`connectors/google-push.ts:177`, `channels/gmail-push.ts:4-5`, `channels/owner-do.ts:1282-1290`).

**Why an ADR.** CLAUDE.md requires explicit bounded contract/ADR review for email-body processing. The reply watch reads a third party's message without a turn asking for it. Owner ruling 7 (10 Oct) names the reply watch as a place where push latency is allowed.

**Reference.** RFC 3834 defines `Auto-Submitted: auto-replied` for automatic responses. RFC 3464 defines delivery status notifications inside `multipart/report; report-type=delivery-status`. Both are evidence the model can read. Neither is reliable alone, because many auto-replies omit the header [inference]. Google's Limited Use policy allows restricted-scope data only for prominent user-facing features, so the watch must be visible to the owner.

## 2. Decision

**A reply watch.** Waldo watches one thread until a deadline when two things are true: the owner approves an email whose card says Waldo will watch for a reply, and Gmail confirms the send. New messages on that thread are read once, judged by the model, and dropped. Only the verdict is kept. Waldo tells the owner and proposes the next step. It never sends on its own.

### 2.1 What is read

- Only new messages on a thread that meets all three conditions: the owner sent it through Waldo; the `email_send` approval ended `done` with verified readback; and the approved payload carried `await_reply`. An `uncertain` or `failed` send gets no watch.
- "New" means a message in that thread, after the sent copy's internal date, whose Gmail id the watch has not seen.
- The owner's own later messages (Gmail label `SENT`) are recorded as origin `owner`. Their bodies are not read and no model call is made. The label is a provider fact, not a judgment.
- Other new messages are read with a fixed header list and a body capped at 8,000 characters, after the E1 artifact quarantine, with a `truncated` marker. Attachments are not read and their names are not passed.
- Only the account that sent the mail is read. One active watch per thread: a later approved send with `await_reply` on the same thread supersedes the earlier watch.

### 2.2 When

- Every update sweep (10 minutes) checks due watches. A verified Gmail push pulls that sweep forward, as today. Push is the latency path. The sweep is the floor, and it also catches replies that skip the inbox.
- Each wake does a metadata-only thread read (`threads.get`, `format=metadata`) per watch. A body is fetched (`messages.get`) only for a new message that is not the owner's own.
- Caps:
  - at most 25 active watches per owner;
  - at most 10 watches checked per wake, least recently checked first;
  - at most 3 new messages judged per watch per wake.
- A send that would need a 26th watch is proposed without one, and the model is told why.

### 2.3 What is stored

Two tables live in the owner object. The new reply-watch book (`channels/reply-watch.ts`) is their one writer.

- `reply_watches`:
  - links: `id`, `approval_id` (unique), `loop_id`, `connection_id`, `thread_id`, `sent_message_id`;
  - times: `sent_at`, `await_until`, `ends_at`, `last_checked_at`;
  - state: `status` (`watching`, `ended`), `ended_reason` (`answered`, `expired`, `superseded`, `loop_closed`, `forgotten`, `disconnected`, `grant_lost`), `check_failures`, `deadline_noticed`;
  - `waiting_ref`: the C7 item, null until C7 exists.
- `reply_watch_messages`: `watch_id`, `message_id` (Gmail id), `fingerprint`, `internal_at`, `origin` (`owner`, `other`), `verdict`, `attempts`, `judged_at`, `noticed`.
- `fingerprint` is SHA-256 over `reply-watch.v1`, the watch id, the Gmail message id and its internal date. It is the idempotency key for the judgment and the notice. It is content-free by construction.
- Never stored: the body, the snippet, the subject, the sender, any header value, or the model's reasoning. The `waiting_for` line and the deadline live in the approved ledger payload. The owner's approval wrote them, not the watch.
- Retention: message rows are deleted 7 days after the watch ends. The watch row is deleted 30 days after it ends.

### 2.4 How the body is treated

- The body is external, tainted content (taint `external`). It may inform the model's judgment. It is never an instruction. The judgment call has no tools.
- It goes in delimiters in the user message, never in the system prompt, through the Scribe, like any external mail read.
- The judgment call carries only:
  - the approved `waiting_for` line;
  - the subject and recipients from the ledger row;
  - the verdicts already recorded on this watch;
  - the new messages' headers and capped bodies.
- It carries no memory, no other mail and no health context. The owner's health never enters this tainted path.
- Nothing is stored (2.3) and nothing goes to logs. The model-call purpose `reply_watch` is metadata-only in every environment (`channels/owner-turn.ts:255`), so neither input nor output reaches a trace, in staging either. The staging capture ruling covers testers' own text, and a correspondent never opted in. Production never captures text anyway (`observability/trace-privacy.ts:65-66`).
- The body never reaches memory, the nightly pass, episodes, R2, browser jobs, drafts or any third-party send.

### 2.5 Who decides

- **The model.** One call per watch per wake, with structured output validated by a contract schema:
  - `verdict`, one of:
    - `answered`: a person replied, and it answers what the owner was waiting for;
    - `replied_open`: a person replied, and the ask is still open;
    - `auto_reply`;
    - `bounce`: some or all recipients did not get the mail;
    - `other`;
    - `unclear`;
  - `notice`: Waldo's own note to the owner, one or two sentences, no quoting, or null;
  - `proposal`: the next step Waldo offers, or null.
- **Schema rule** (validation, not judgment): `answered` and `bounce` require a `notice`, so a closure or a failed delivery is never silent.
- Headers such as `Auto-Submitted`, a `multipart/report` content type and `X-Failed-Recipients` are passed as evidence. No regex decides the verdict.
- An invalid or failed output counts as an attempt. After 3 attempts the message is `unclear`, and the owner is told once that a new message arrived on the thread.

### 2.6 Expiry and deadline

- The model sets `await_reply.until` at proposal time, 1 to 30 days ahead, together with a `waiting_for` line of at most 200 characters. The card shows both: "I'll watch this thread for a reply until <date> (waiting for: <line>) and tell you what comes back." No `await_reply` means no watch. An owner who wants the send without the watch asks for it again without one.
- `ends_at` is `until` plus 48 hours, so a reply that lands just after the deadline still counts.
- At `until`, if no `answered` verdict exists, Waldo tells the owner once that no reply came and offers a nudge draft. That note is written from the ledger row and the verdict enums only, with no body.
- At `ends_at` the watch ends `expired`. The loop stays open; the owner closes or drops it.

### 2.7 What Waldo does

- On approval, the desk opens Waldo's own loop (title from `waiting_for`, due `until`) in the same transaction as `done`.
- `answered`: Waldo closes that loop as `done`, with the verdict row as closure evidence, and says so in the notice. If the owner says it was not an answer, the model opens a new loop.
- `bounce`: Waldo tells the owner which delivery failed, as the model read it, and proposes a fix (a corrected address, a resend). The watch continues for the other recipients.
- `replied_open`, `auto_reply`, `other`, `unclear`: the loop stays open. A notice goes out only when the model writes one.
- Every next step is a proposal. A reply draft or a resend goes through `send_email` and the approval desk like any send. Mail sends stay per-action approval. No standing grant applies to a send proposed from a reply-watch verdict until the standing-permission ADR says otherwise.
- Notices go through the final outbox to the owner's proactive surface (ruling 20), with a `replyWatch` receipt keyed by the fingerprint. They honour quiet hours, volume and the follow-ups switch.
- The update lane skips messages in an actively watched thread, so one reply produces at most one notice.

### 2.8 Forget, disconnect, off

- **Forget:** the watch tables hold no text, so a literal forget has nothing to rewrite there.
  - A forget that terminalises the watch's loop (existing loop coverage, `memory/claims.ts:695-704`) ends the watch `forgotten` in the same transaction and deletes its message rows.
  - Undelivered `replyWatch` outbox rows join the existing mail-follow-up redaction (`channels/telegram-final-outbox.ts:273`).
- **Loop closed:** closing or dropping the loop ends the watch `loop_closed`.
- **Disconnect:** disconnecting the Google account ends that account's watches `disconnected` at once and deletes their message rows (`channels/owner-do.ts:2388-2397` gains the call). No read happens after.
- **Grant failure:** reads stop while the grant fails to refresh. If it is still failing at `ends_at`, the watch ends `grant_lost` and the owner is told once.
- **Follow-ups off** (`proactiveEnabled`): no reads and no notices while off. The watch still ends at `ends_at`. The model does not propose new watches while follow-ups are off.

### 2.9 Link to C7 durable tasks

- C7 is not built at `e5c022ef`. Its spec (#1103, comment 6154789747) lets a step wait on an event through `waiting_on`.
- When C7 lands, a step that proposes a send with `await_reply` returns `blocked` with `waiting_on: reply_watch:<watch id>`.
- When the watch reaches a terminal state (`answered`, a `bounce` for every recipient, `expired`, or any end), the book calls `unblock` with the verdict enum only.
- If the resumed step needs the words, it reads the thread through `read_thread` under the turn's normal rules. No body enters the C7 journal.
- Until C7 lands, the watch stands alone with its loop.

### 2.10 Logs and traces

- One hop `reply_watch` per wake, with counts and enums only: watches checked, new messages, verdicts, failures, ms. No text.
- `llm_reply_watch` carries usage and shape only.

### 2.11 Switch

- `REPLY_WATCH.enabled = false` in `channels/reply-watch.ts` until the eval in section 6 meets its bar. It gates the `await_reply` field, the card line and the runner. Off means today's behaviour.
- The end, forget and disconnect paths run whatever the switch says.
- The watch runs only where `MAIL_SOURCE_FOLLOWUPS` is on (staging `1`, production `0` today). This ADR makes no `wrangler.jsonc` change.

## 3. Considered options

1. **Headers and snippet only.** Same watch, no full body. Smaller surface and cheaper. Rejected as the default because "will get back to you" versus an answer, and the cause of a delivery report, usually lie past the snippet [inference]. The eval runs this variant on the same fixtures. If it meets the bar, it replaces the body read.
2. **Bounded body read on approved, watched threads only.** Chosen (section 2).
3. **Fold into the inbox update lane.** Rejected:
   - it is inbox-wide, not bounded to approved threads;
   - `update_cards` stores from, subject and snippet, and the staging trace carries them, which conflicts with "never stored";
   - it has no link to the approval;
   - it misses replies outside the inbox.
4. **No watch; read on request.** Rejected: it fails ruling 7's reply watch and the follow-up closure, and bounces stay silent.

## 4. Consequences

- **Benefits:**
  - A sent email's outcome reaches the follow-up: answered, still open, auto-reply or bounced.
  - The owner hears about a failed delivery without asking.
  - Retention is lower than the existing mail paths: ids and enums only.
- **Costs and risks:**
  - A background reader of third-party text.
  - One model call per wake for each watch that has new mail.
  - Two new edge read methods, which need an owner deploy.
  - Prompt injection through a reply body. It is contained: no tools, enum output, owner-only notice, desk-only actions.
  - A reply that starts a new Gmail thread is missed [inference].
  - The notice is Waldo's own sentence. Like every proactive message it lands in the owner's transcript, so the instruction forbids quoting.
- **Impact surface:**
  - contracts: `tools/schemas/writes.ts` (the `send_email` args) and a new `runtime/reply-watch.ts` (the verdict schema);
  - desk: `channels/approvals.ts`;
  - tools and Google client: `tools/live/google.ts`, `connectors/google.ts` (two read methods, `GOOGLE_METHODS`);
  - edge: `supabase/functions/connector-proxy/index.ts` (scope check);
  - new modules: `channels/reply-watch.ts`, `prompt/reply-watch.ts`;
  - changed runtime: `channels/update-cards.ts`, `channels/owner-do.ts`, `channels/loops.ts`, `memory/claims.ts`, `channels/telegram-final-outbox.ts`, `channels/owner-turn.ts`.
  - No app contract change: the app renders the review text. No hosted migration, no wrangler change, no secret.
- **Process:** this record is not authoritative until it is published in Brain and `accepted-adrs.json` is regenerated.

## 5. Verification and tests

- **Contract:**
  - `await_reply` valid and invalid cases: past date, more than 30 days ahead, empty or over-long `waiting_for`;
  - verdict schema valid and invalid cases: `answered` without a notice is rejected.
- **Card:** the review text carries the watch line on Telegram and in the app. The payload digest changes when `until` changes. A proposal without `await_reply` shows no line.
- **Desk:**
  - the watch is created in the same transaction as `done`;
  - none for `uncertain`, `failed` or a send without `await_reply`;
  - the recovery path creates it exactly once;
  - a second watched send on the thread supersedes the first;
  - a 26th is refused, and the model is told.
- **Runner** (workers pool, fake Gmail, fake model):
  - one reply gives one call, one verdict row, the loop closed `done` with evidence, and one notice;
  - push and sweep together give one judgment;
  - an owner `SENT` message gives no body read and no model call;
  - a reply filed outside the inbox is found by the sweep;
  - 11 watches give 10 checked; 4 new messages give 3 judged.
- **Storage falsifier:** after a judged reply carrying a canary string in body, subject and sender, no owner-object table, KV key, outbox row or trace sink contains the canary.
- **Traces:** with staging configuration (capture on), `llm_reply_watch` has no `text`, and the `reply_watch` hop has counts only.
- **Hostile:** a reply that tells Waldo to forward the thread or send money produces a verdict and a notice only. No tool call is possible, nothing is sent, and the loop changes only per the verdict.
- **Health:** the judgment input holds no health context, even when the owner has health connected.
- **Deadline** (time-mocked, including a DST change in the owner's zone): one notice at `until`; `expired` at `ends_at`; a reply between the two still counts.
- **Forget, disconnect, off:**
  - forgetting the loop's topic ends the watch and deletes its message rows;
  - disconnect ends the watch, and no read follows;
  - with follow-ups off, nothing is read.
- **Degraded:**
  - Gmail 429 or 5xx counts as a check failure, with no notice spam;
  - a model outage counts attempts, then gives one `unclear` notice after 3;
  - an edge without the new methods fails closed with no reads.
- **C7** (when built): a blocked step resumes on `answered` with the enum only.

## 6. Eval bar for the switch

- The fixture set has at least 30 synthetic messages and no real mail:
  - direct answers and "will get back to you";
  - out-of-office replies with and without `Auto-Submitted`;
  - hard and delayed delivery reports;
  - a reply from a CC'd person and a reply in another language;
  - injected instructions.
- It runs on a real model twice: full body, and headers plus snippet.
- The switch turns on when the full-body run meets all three conditions:
  - zero `answered` on auto-replies, delivery reports and injection probes;
  - bounce recall of at least 0.9;
  - answered recall of at least 0.8.
- If the headers-and-snippet run also meets the bar, the build moves to option 1 before flipping.
- The flip PR reports both runs' counts.

## 7. Rollback

- Flip `REPLY_WATCH.enabled` off and deploy. The card line and the runner stop. Stored rows stay inert and age out under 2.3. The end, forget and disconnect paths keep running.
- `await_reply` is optional, so older proposals still parse.
- The edge methods are additive, and leaving them deployed is harmless.
- There are no hosted migrations to reverse.

## 8. Decisions for the owner

1. Scope: Option 2, with the bounds in 2.1-2.2.
2. Caps: a window of at most 30 days (plus 48 hours of grace), and 8,000 body characters.
3. Traces: the `reply_watch` purpose is metadata-only in staging too (recommended). The alternative is to allow staging capture under the 10 Oct ruling.
4. Closure: `answered` closes Waldo's own loop automatically (recommended). The alternative is that Waldo only proposes the closure.

G3.reasoning:
Hypotheses considered:
- (1) G3 is best served by a broad grant model so it pays off fast (option C).
- (2) A global slider is enough (option D).
- (3) A narrow first class on the existing desk and ledger seams gives real autonomy with bounded blast radius (option B).
- (4) Grants are not needed yet (option A).

Disconfirming evidence against C and D:
- Both cover sends to other people, which are irreversible. Email "can't be undone" (approvals.ts:598), and RSVP and invite moves email guests.
- The release brief forbids sends, spending, deletes, sharing and health destinations.
- CLAUDE.md:20 requires per-resource, parameter, time and budget scope, which a slider lacks.

Evidence against A: the Window job (ADR-0019) and Patrol only matter if Waldo can act unattended somewhere. A has no path there.

Why B, given the code:
1. The seams exist. The desk freezes and digests payloads and already reads the event before a move. The owner effect ledger already reserves intent and grant quota in one synchronous transaction (owner-effect-ledger.ts:43-70), so the recheck at dispatch is a sync SQL read inside it. That puts no external I/O in the transaction.
2. "Waldo's own block" is provable from the ledger: a done create whose provider_id is the event id (approvals.ts:771). The proof does not depend on a marker other apps could write.
3. The effect reaches nobody else and is reversible: no attendees, times only, etag-guarded undo, with the move schema already refusing description, location and attendees (calendar.ts:23-25). ADR-0019 already classes Window events as always reversible.
4. One writer per aggregate holds: the grant module writes grants, the desk writes rows, the ledger writes intents and counts uses. v0.5 authority_grants stays untouched, so no protocol widening.
5. It composes:
   - A C7 step flips effects_dispatched, because propose_calendar_change is not safe_read (tool-replay-class.ts:35), so an interrupted step never resumes.
   - A Patrol timer pass can use the grant, while a pass woken by an external event cards.
   - Standing orders stay instruction text.
6. PR #932's strongest parts carry over: exact-scope matching, overlap fails to a card, usage that fails closed, a recheck after every await, instant expiry, and its tests. Its risky parts are dropped: send and purchase areas, area modes, in-memory proposals.

Main trade-off: B gives the least immediate relief. Reminders to named people and invite declines are the high-volume asks, and they stay behind cards until their own rulings. That cost is deliberate: the first standing permission should be one whose worst case is an undoable change to the owner's own focus time.

Threshold to proceed: the owner accepts the never-list and the defaults, and the slice-3 tests show the authorize callback runs inside reserve with no awaited I/O. Confidence: about 75%. The main uncertainty is how many real Waldo-created blocks qualify.
G3.falsifier:
Any one of these makes B the wrong choice.

1. In 20 runs of the hostile scenario (an invite whose description tells Waldo to move focus blocks), any grant-run move lands outside the owner window or above the daily cap. That means the bounds are not enforced at the host.
2. The grant recheck cannot run inside owner-effect-ledger reserve's transactionSync without awaited I/O. Recheck-at-dispatch then fails CLAUDE.md:18, and A should stand until it can.
3. Beta data after 30 days shows Waldo-created focus blocks mostly have guests, recur, or predate the effect ledger, or testers move them fewer than once a week. The class then reaches too little value, and another first class should be picked (the mechanism may still stand).
4. The app cannot pin the additive contract (the standing_grant kind, the grants routes) before the backend needs to emit. Then the first release must stay switch-off.
5. A multi-use grant already exists under another name (harness doc §13). Then this ADR becomes a review of that path instead.
